analysis:
The PR removes the retained console lane from repo tooling and does not touch runtime provider code, crypto, attestation, the coordinator WebSocket contract, or the cache. Changes by file:

- TelemetrySymmetryTests.swift: a doc-comment edit only (lines 9-10).
- scripts/ci-component-paths.py: COMPONENTS is now only ("provider",) at line 13, and the CONSOLE patterns and the console selection are removed. COMMON still forces every component on for shared files, and the provider PATTERNS are unchanged. Path classification still uses NUL-delimited git diff output with full-SHA validation, so no new injection surface appears. Default-branch pushes and new branches still run the full set.
- scripts/docs-check.sh: comment only (lines 170-173). CITE_ROOTS and historical_source_exists are unchanged, so behavior is identical.
- scripts/docs-impact-rules.json: the console rules and the console-ui telemetry-types source pattern are removed. This only narrows doc-impact enforcement for paths that no longer exist in this repo. The provider privacy and trust rule, which maps to docs/threat-model.yaml, is unchanged.
- scripts/test-ci-component-paths.py: the patch excerpt is truncated, but the visible hunks adjust the tests to match. They remove the console assertions and add a newline-in-filename test that checks the NUL-delimited diff handling. They also tighten the forbidden-string check on provider workflows to include console-ui/.

One uncertainty remains. The ci.yml, component-changes.yml and ci-related workflow changes are not in this batch. If ci.yml still references needs.<classifier>.outputs.console or a console job, that could break or skip CI, but that is outside the supplied evidence. No threat-model assets (A-001..A-018), boundaries (TB-002/003/007/009/011/012) or threats (T-041 etc.) are affected.
